title: Forget "Malaise 2.0," GM says it's still all-in on EVs and autonomy
gist: At GM Forward, GM said it will expand hands-off, eyes-off Super Cruise to nearly every vehicle, launched OnStar AI and a Gen-4 EV architecture on cheaper LMR batteries, and framed customer trust, including end-to-end encrypted dash cam video, as central to its AI and autonomy plans.

insights.claim: GM will expand its hands-off, eyes-off Super Cruise to nearly every vehicle including pickup trucks and crossovers, not just last year's Escalade IQ, and is testing the technology at 1 million miles a month in virtual and real worlds.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Broad Super Cruise rollout turns autonomy into a lineup-wide software feature.
insights.locator: At this year’s GM Forward event

insights.claim: GM's VP of Autonomous Vehicles Rashed Haq says GM judges Level 4 readiness on safety and roadcraft, and GM expects responsibility to fall on GM and the computer when a malfunction occurs while the car is driving.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Manufacturer liability acceptance for Level 4 is a key adoption and cost variable.
insights.locator: “We look at two key factors, safety and roadcraft,”

insights.claim: GM shuttered Cruise and mothballed its robotaxis but continues to work on autonomous vehicles, with a longer-term vision of cars doing tasks like picking up dry cleaning or driving a child to school.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: GM is pivoting from robotaxis to consumer-owned autonomy.

insights.claim: GM's OnStar AI is a specialized assistant trained on the car's details, can explain alerts and place pickup orders from learned habits, and runs largely locally thanks to new central compute, which GM says other models such as Gemini cannot match.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: In-vehicle AI is GM's attempt to own the customer interface rather than cede it to Google.
insights.locator: GM’s newly announced OnStar AI will play a role

insights.claim: GM executive Sterling Anderson argues people trust their cars more than their phones, so a car suggesting a favorite restaurant in context may be more accepted.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Trust differential supports in-car commerce and services.
insights.quote: People have a relationship with their cars that they don’t have with other things

insights.claim: GM's new infotainment dash cam function uploads video to GM's cloud with end-to-end encryption, so GM cannot decrypt it and could not hand it to law enforcement.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Privacy-by-design addresses a risk given GM's past data selling.

insights.claim: GM was previously found to be selling customers' data, often without their knowledge, to insurance companies, which the author says makes the new trust posture notable.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Past data practices make trust claims subject to proof.
insights.locator: That is the type of trust that is absolutely needed

insights.claim: GM wants to keep customers in its ecosystem, with a two-GM-car household where OnStar AI could reroute the closer spouse to complete an errand.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Ecosystem lock-in is the strategic aim of connected services.
insights.locator: GM also wants to keep customers within its own ecosystem.

themes.theme: Gen-4 EV architecture and LMR batteries

insights.claim: GM announced a Gen-4 EV architecture based on lithium manganese-rich (LMR) batteries, with energy densities close to nickel-manganese-cobalt but without cobalt, bringing cost closer to LFP cells.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Cheaper chemistry is GM's path to affordable EVs despite the expired US tax credit.
insights.locator: GM also announced its Gen-4 EV architecture

insights.claim: The LMR cells are expected to make batteries about 30 percent cheaper, helping GM offer a wider range of EVs including affordable models like the limited-run Bolt.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: Battery cost reduction is key to EV margins in a weak US incentive environment.

insights.claim: GM is positioning itself against a perception of Malaise 2.0 in US EV adoption, citing the expiration of the EV tax credit and the rest of the world's embrace of EVs.
insights.speaker: Ars Contributors
insights.so_what: US EV demand headwinds from policy are the backdrop for GM's investment messaging.
insights.locator: It’s easy to criticize US automakers
